studio.label: Studio
studio.title: About HAZEON
studio.text: We take on a few projects at a time and put experienced engineers on each one. AI speeds up the repetitive work: tests, migrations, boilerplate. The decisions stay with people, and everything we build is yours.
studio.f1label: First call. Free, and you leave with a technical roadmap.
studio.f2label: Between two live demos of your product.
studio.f3label: Of the code, designs and IP belong to you.
studio.f4label: Signed before you share any details.

anatomy.label: What we build
anatomy.title: What goes into a product we ship.
anatomy.lead: Most of the work is invisible to the people using it. Here is a typical product, layer by layer, and what we take care of at each level.
anatomy.l1text: Web and mobile apps that load fast and are easy to use. Design systems, accessibility and analytics included.
anatomy.l2text: Your business rules as clean, tested code, with documented APIs that other teams can build on.
anatomy.l3text: Assistants, agents and automations with guardrails, evaluations and cost limits, so answers stay grounded.
anatomy.l4text: Databases, pipelines and vector search, modeled so the product can grow without a rewrite.
anatomy.l5text: Cloud setup, CI/CD, monitoring, backups and security checks on every commit.

services.label: Services
services.title: Six things we do well.
services.lead: Each one comes with experienced engineers, a demo every week and code that belongs to you.
services.s1text: Assistants that answer from your own documents, agents that take repetitive back-office work off your team, and the evaluations that prove they work.
services.s2text: From an idea to a product people can sign up for. Tight scope, clean code, and a codebase that can grow with you.
services.s3text: Multi-tenant platforms, dashboards and customer portals. Billing, roles, permissions and audit logs: the unglamorous parts, done properly.
services.s4text: Threat modeling, secret scanning, dependency audits and penetration tests. Security is part of the build, not a checkbox at the end.
services.s5text: Infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, containers and monitoring. Releasing on a Friday should be boring.
services.s6text: We move old, fragile codebases to modern stacks one piece at a time, tests first, without stopping the business.

assistant.label: Inside a build
assistant.title: How an AI assistant answers from your documents.
assistant.lead: It's the system we get asked for most. Here is what happens between a question and an answer you can trust.
assistant.n1text: PDFs, Notion, Drive, tickets or your own database.
assistant.n2text: Documents become passages, passages become vectors.
assistant.n3text: Stored in a vector database, with the same access rules as the source.
assistant.n4text: The passages closest to the question are pulled back.
assistant.n5text: The model writes an answer using only those passages.
assistant.n6text: Guardrails check the answer and attach its sources.
assistant.question: Can customers on an annual plan get a refund?
assistant.answer: Yes, within 30 days of purchase. After that, the unused months are refunded pro rata.

process.label: Process
process.title: A typical MVP, week by week.
process.lead: Your timeline depends on scope. After the first call, you get a real one, in writing.
process.p1text: A 15-minute call, then a workshop on goals, users and constraints. You get a written roadmap.
process.p2text: A clickable prototype and the system design, agreed on before any production code is written.
process.p3text: One-week sprints. At the end of each one, you see a live demo of working software.
process.p4text: Automated tests run on every change, and a security review closes the build.
process.p5text: Production release with monitoring in place, and us on call for the first days.
process.p6text: We keep improving the product with you, or hand it over with full documentation.

stack.label: Stack
stack.title: Proven tools, chosen per project.
stack.lead: We pick what your team can maintain after we leave, not what's trending this month.

engage.label: Working together
engage.title: Three ways to work with us.
engage.lead: Every project starts with a free 15-minute call and a written plan. Then you choose.
engage.m1how: Fixed scope, a live demo every week
engage.m1get: A launched product and all of its code
engage.m2for: Teams that need more experienced hands
engage.m2how: Our engineers join your tools and rituals
engage.m3get: A ranked list of automations and a working first agent

careers.label: Careers
careers.title: Do your final-year project with us.
careers.lead: Five end-of-studies internships (PFE), each one on a real product. An experienced engineer reviews your work every day, and the goal is to ship it.
careers.perk3: Modern AI stack: LLMs, RAG, agents
careers.perk4: Your own scope from week one
careers.r1text: Build an enterprise assistant that lets people chat with company documents, with answers that always cite their sources. You'll own the chunking strategy, retrieval quality and the guardrails against off-topic answers.
careers.r2text: Build an agent that refactors like a senior engineer: it reads legacy Python, plans the change, writes modern TypeScript and checks its own work before a human reviews it.
careers.r3text: Build an AI producer for video creators: from one niche, it researches trends, analyzes them with LLMs and drafts data-backed video plans, all in one SaaS workflow.
careers.r4text: Build a screening assistant for recruiters that pre-processes video interviews (speech clarity, keywords, sentiment) so they can focus on the right candidates first.
careers.r5text: Build the engine of an automated code reviewer: deterministic rules catch leaked secrets, LLMs flag code smells, all before a pull request is merged.
careers.h1text: Send your CV and GitHub, and tell us what you like building.
careers.h2text: A five-day challenge based on a real MVP. No trick puzzles.
careers.h3text: Walk us through your decisions and the trade-offs you made.
careers.h4text: You start shipping, with a mentor from day one.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Questions we often get.
faq.lead: Something else on your mind? Ask us and an engineer will reply.
faq.q1: How fast can you deliver an MVP?
faq.a1: Most MVPs take between six and ten weeks, depending on scope. After the first call you get a technical roadmap with a realistic timeline, before you commit to anything.
faq.q2: Who owns the code and the IP?
faq.a2: You do, entirely. Source code, designs, infrastructure and documentation are yours from the first day. No lock-in.
faq.q3: How do you use AI in development?
faq.a3: AI handles repetitive work like boilerplate, tests and migrations, so engineers can spend their time on architecture and quality. A person reviews every line, and your confidential data never goes to third-party tools without your approval.
faq.q4: Can you work with our existing team and systems?
faq.a4: Yes. We join existing codebases, modernize legacy systems step by step and work with the tools your team already uses.
faq.q5: How much does a project cost?
faq.a5: It depends on scope, complexity and timeline. MVP sprints are fixed-price, dedicated teams are billed monthly. After a free call, we send you a clear estimate.
faq.a6: Yes, gladly. We can sign one before you share any details about your idea.
